name: MotoJava
landmarks: Next to the Dainese store, across from Tap Plastics. Two blocks off Market Street.
hours_summary: Tue to Fri 11 am to 6 pm. Sat 12 pm to 5 pm. Sun and Mon by appointment.

financing.heading: Financing on every bike
financing.text: Installment loans through Roadrunner Financial. Terms from 12 to 60 months, rates from 9.9%.

fees.heading: Tax, title and fees
fees.text: Sales tax and registration are the same as at the DMV. Title transfer is $15. Our $85 documentation fee covers a DMV runner who stands in line for you.

tow.heading: Tow-in special
tow.text: San Francisco $99, East Bay $150. For service or a bike purchase. Delivery is available.

services.name: Annual maintenance
services.text: Keeps the bike running the way it should now and later. Scope varies by make and model, call for specifics.

services.name: Full service
services.text: Everything in an annual service and much more. Varies by make and model.

services.name: Oil change
services.text: Regular oil changes prevent problems and extend the life of the engine.

services.name: Repairs
services.text: If something feels different, getting it checked sooner usually costs less and saves time.

services.name: Tire change
services.text: Mounting and balancing. Bring your own tires or buy through us.

service_intro: We check and maintain a steady flow of our own bikes, so the shop is set up for yours too. Annual maintenance, full service, oil changes, tires and repairs. As a small shop we are usually booked about a week out.

why.title: Inspected and serviced
why.text: Every bike gets a tune-up, a 37-point inspection and a safety check before it goes on the floor.

why.title: Paperwork handled
why.text: We prepare the DMV title transfer and registration so you skip the line.

why.title: Fair and firm
why.text: Prices are set fairly and stay there. Taxes and fees are extra and explained up front.

stats.label: New riders started on a Nighthawk 250

team.name: Mike Ritter
team.bio: Mike has ridden for more than 25 years and toured in 46 countries. He has been a shop mechanic, a salesman and a certified riding instructor, and ran his own school, Moto Mike Learn to Ride. If you are new to riding, Mike is the person to talk to.

team.name: Kim Danner
team.bio: Kim came to riding later than Mike and took to it fast. She runs the shop with him and still says learning to ride was an easy choice.

citybike.text: Mike's first bike was a Honda Spree scooter he bought at 14 while shopping for a car. He named it Killing Spree. From there came a KZ440, an XS650 and a Honda 400/4 he still owns. He wrenched at Scuderia while in culinary school, sold bikes at Motorcycles Unlimited, became an MSF instructor and started his own school. He has toured 46 countries, including a year in Europe on a Yamaha Fazer and nine trips to the Isle of Man. At MotoJava he estimates more than 700 Nighthawk 250s have passed through his hands to new riders.

directions.text: Take US 101 North to exit 434A for Mission Street. Turn right on Plum Street, then left on Van Ness. We are on the right, across from Tap Plastics.
Keep left for the Central Freeway toward Civic Center, then exit 434A for Mission Street. Right on Plum, left on Van Ness.
